sections.title: About Your Role
paras: This role supports Harrison.ai Services, which provides non-clinical services, including operations support, to Frontier Radiology, a US teleradiology practice.

The Client Implementation & Account Manager owns getting new client facilities live — and then keeps them healthy. This is primarily an implementation role: you lead every aspect of the new site go-live process, from the handoff at contract signature through stable production, and you are the client's working-level single point of contact throughout. Once a site is running, you remain their named relationship owner for service performance and escalations. You hold a named book of accounts; the VP of Operations retains a portfolio of their own and executive sponsorship across all accounts.

This is an implementation and account management role. You do not build interfaces or configure systems: every workstream in a go-live — contract scope, IT implementation, credentialing, radiologist onboarding, clinical workflow, staffing and coverage, billing setup, support and monitoring — has an owning function. You own the go-live date and the gaps between them: the right people convened, scope agreed, sequence held, nothing dropped between functions. You will run concurrent implementations and hold ongoing relationships with live facilities.

sections.title: What You Do:
bullets: Own the client go-live process for your book of accounts, within the operating model set by the VP of Operations, and improve it as volume grows.

Run the internal handoff from Sales and lead client kickoff: validate that what was sold is what will be delivered, bring IT implementation and the other owning functions into discovery with the client, and surface gaps before the client hears about them.

Coordinate integration requirements between the client's technical team and our IT team — convene the right people, make sure requirements are captured and documented, confirm both sides agree on scope, and keep the build unblocked.

Build and own the implementation project plan, including the credentialing and state-licensure critical path; set firm go-live dates and milestones, hold the project team and client to them, and escalate to the VP of Operations when the plan is at risk.

Coordinate and drive testing with the client and IT: end-to-end validation, patient demographic and accession integrity, image and priors verification, report delivery confirmation, and workflow dry runs with their staff.

Coordinate user provisioning, client-side training, and reference documentation, including ongoing technologist adds and removals for live sites; lead go-live with coverage confirmed, escalation tree published, and the hypercare window staffed and monitored.
Close out with a documented configuration record and formal transition to steady state; maintain and improve the implementation playbook, runbooks, and client configuration records.

Serve as named relationship owner and working-level single point of contact for your live facilities; deliver quarterly business reviews grounded in performance data — turnaround time, study volume, and SLA attainment.

Direct experience with a distributed reading model — teleradiology, a multi-site radiology group with centralized or remote interpretation, an outsourced or overflow reading arrangement, or a health system routing studies across facilities for interpretation.
Hands-on experience bringing new facilities, sites, or reading arrangements live, including credentialing and licensure sequencing, workflow design, and go-live execution.

sections.title: About the role
paras: Pricing is where mortgage deals are won or lost. A few basis points can decide whether a borrower gets the loan and whether our customers win the business. Our goal is the best pricing in the market, and we want to approach it with the rigor of a top hedge fund, using data, models, and a constant read on what the market is doing.

We’re hiring a Lead PM to own Capital Markets and Pricing. You’ll own how loans get priced, locked, and sold, from the rate a borrower sees to how the loan is executed in the secondary market. Because Pylon is vertically integrated, we can cut out a lot of the manual work and margin leakage that traditional lenders just accept, and pass those savings on to borrowers.
You’ll also build products that set us apart. That means finding gaps in the market, designing loan programs for borrowers others underserve, and launching them with our capital partners.

Get us to the best pricing in the market by automating best execution across agency cash and MBS, aggregators, and whole loan buyers
Build pricing models and strategies with the rigor of a hedge fund, watching rate moves, spreads, investor appetite, and competitor pricing, and turning what you see into better prices
Write and ship code yourself, from pricing models and analysis to changes in the pricing engine
Design loan products competitors can’t easily copy, and work with investors and capital partners to bring them to market
Make pricing real-time and available through our API, so customers get every price, adjustment, and eligibility decision instantly, with a clear explanation behind each one
Cut cost and leakage across the loan lifecycle, including pull-through, lock extensions, fallout, pricing exceptions, and repurchase risk

You care a lot about our customers and their borrowers. Better pricing means real money saved for real families, and we’ll do whatever it takes to make our customers successful.

You’re obsessed with how the market moves. You follow rates, spreads, and investor behavior closely, you always want to know why things moved, and you’re always looking for ways to price better because of it.

You default to software over manual work. One of our guiding principles is that anything in the backend mortgage process done by a human is a bug, and capital markets still runs on a lot of spreadsheets, phone calls, and manual reconciliation. When we need a temporary workaround, you flag it, write it down, and push for the real fix.

Trillions of dollars in fund assets sit idle in settlement delays and collateral buffers because no rail can move legal title in real time. We are building that rail on the XRP Ledger, and it is already live: tokenized funds exist on XRPL today as Multi-Purpose Tokens (MPTs), moving as collateral across issuance, distribution and repo with some of the world's largest asset managers and custodians.
You will own the two protocol workstreams that decide how far this goes.

Token standards. MPTs need to grow from a fund token into a complete issuance framework for institutions: asset restrictions, corporate events, programmable behavior. Get this right and the next wave of assets (commercial paper, commodities, bonds, equities) can be issued, held and mobilized natively on a public ledger. Each asset class brings its own rules, and you will determine what fits within the protocol and what remains outside it.

sections.title: WHAT YOU’LL DO:
paras: In your first 90 days, you will take charge of a single roadmap across tokenization and privacy and know every open item on it. By the end of your first year, you will have successfully delivered the next generation of tokenization capabilities. And outlined what institutional privacy on XRPL entails.
bullets: Lead the tokenization roadmap for XRPL: MPT evolution, transfer controls, corporate actions and programmable tokens, and decide what belongs in the protocol versus above it.
Lead the privacy roadmap: take Confidential MPTs from mainnet launch to institutional scale, including key rotation and recovery, performance targets and confidential vaults.
Generate new feature specifications and build the consensus behind them, working with Ripple engineering, XRPL validators and open-source contributors to carry proposals from concept to amendment.
Set the requirements and priorities for each new asset class, and shape the go-to-market that brings capital markets participants onto XRPL.
Make new primitives usable, not just live: bring hardware wallets, custodians and issuer platforms along so institutions can adopt on day one.
Scope the compliance capabilities that regulated issuers need to meet their obligations on XRPL.
Partner with developer growth and documentation teams so institutions can originate assets on XRPL without a Ripple engineer in the room.
Define the metrics that show the work is landing: XRPL's share of tokenized assets, issuance volume and ecosystem integrations.

sections.title: Summary:
paras: Every application on ZipRecruiter comes out of two things: what we know about a job seeker, and the flow they go through to apply. The profile holds that knowledge: resume, work history, skills, preferences, and the trade-offs that matter in their job search. The apply flow turns interest in a job into an application an employer can act on. Together they decide how many job seekers who find a job they like go on to apply, and how well each application represents the person behind it.

You will own Product for both. That means deciding what we ask job seekers and when, how we build and keep an accurate picture of each person, and how we get from a job click to a completed, high-quality application with as little effort from the user as possible. The goal is simple to state and hard to deliver: a job seeker should never have to tell us something twice, and every application should show an employer the right reasons to respond.

Few Product roles at ZipRecruiter have more stakeholders. The apply flow is where employer requirements meet the job seeker experience. Employers ask screening questions and rely on applications arriving in their own systems. Trust and safety teams protect the marketplace from fraudulent and low-quality applications. Profile data feeds matching, messaging, and the resume database tools employers use. This is a high-stakes product area where small changes can have outsized impact and there is a huge amount of untapped opportunity for PMs with the ownership and drive to deliver.

sections.title: Key Focuses:
bullets: Act as an Owner: Take full accountability for the job seeker profile and apply flow, from setting KPIs across the funnel to the details of individual screens and questions.

Build the profile job seekers want to keep: Decide what we learn about job seekers, how we learn it, and how we use it to make every later step faster and more accurate. Make the value of a rich profile obvious to the job seeker.

Remove friction from applying: Own conversion from a job click to a started application, and from a started application to a completed one. Know where job seekers drop out, why, and what each question and friction point costs.

Deliver applications employers act on: Partner with employer-side teams on driving application quality, and how applications reach employer systems, so that the most interested and qualified job seekers stand out.

Obsess over your metrics: Apply starts and completions, profile completeness and accuracy, and job seeker retention. You will know how each part of the flow moves them, and you will interrogate the why behind the numbers.
Run on experiments: Design, read, and resolve experiments with judgment about long-term marketplace health, beyond the short-term lift in application volume.

Voice of the Job Seeker: Talk to job seekers, run research, and understand the moment of applying from their side: what they expect, what they will tolerate, and what makes them trust us with their information.

The Role: Strategy is seeking an experienced, execution-focused Public Sector Partner Manager to help build a high-performing partner ecosystem across the public sector, with a primary emphasis on the U.S. Federal Government.

This is not an administrative alliance-management role. It is a field-facing, revenue-producing position responsible for identifying the partners that matter, building joint business plans, aligning partner and Strategy sales teams, and creating measurable pipeline.

The successful candidate will understand the complexities of the federal technology market, including agency buying processes, procurement pathways, contract vehicles, cloud marketplaces, and the role that systems integrators and resellers play in shaping agency modernization programs.

sections.title: Job Description
paras: Working closely with Strategy’s Public Sector sales organization, partner leadership, marketing, solution engineering, and customer success teams, this individual will help insert Strategy Mosaic and Mosaic AI into active agency programs, modernization initiatives, cloud migrations, and enterprise AI opportunities.

The role's mandate will be to build and execute a high-impact public sector partner strategy that generates net-new pipeline, accelerates strategic opportunities, and expands Strategy’s reach across the U.S. Federal Government.

The Public Sector Partner Manager will develop productive relationships with cloud providers, systems integrators, resellers, advisory firms, and technology partners that influence how federal agencies evaluate, procure, implement, and expand enterprise analytics and AI platforms.

sections.title: 1. Federal Partner Strategy and Business Development — 35%
bullets: Develop the Partner Ecosystem: Identify, recruit, and develop strategic systems integrators, resellers, cloud partners, advisory firms, and technology partners capable of expanding Strategy’s federal market presence.

Joint Business Planning: Create actionable business plans with assigned partners, including target agencies, priority accounts, executive relationships, joint solutions, pipeline objectives, enablement requirements, and revenue commitments.
Federal Market Alignment: Align partner strategies to the priorities of federal civilian, Department of Defense, intelligence community, and other public sector organizations.
Partner Prioritization: Focus resources on partners with the relationships, contract access, technical capabilities, and delivery capacity required to generate measurable revenue.
Executive Engagement: Build strong relationships with senior partner executives, public sector practice leaders, account leaders, solution leaders, and government affairs or procurement specialists.

sections.title: 2. Partner-Sourced Pipeline and Co-Selling Execution — 35%
bullets: Generate Pipeline: Develop net-new partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities through account mapping, executive introductions, joint workshops, field events, agency-specific campaigns, and coordinated business development.
Account-Level Co-Selling: Map Strategy’s priority federal accounts against partner relationships, existing programs, contract vehicles, and agency modernization initiatives.

Opportunity Execution: Work alongside Strategy account executives to develop partner strategies for major opportunities, establish clear roles, and use partner influence to improve access, competitive positioning, procurement strategy, and close probability.
Pipeline Governance: Maintain accurate partner opportunity information, sourcing attribution, next steps, forecasts, and partner activity within Strategy’s CRM and partner-management systems.
Forecasting: Provide accurate weekly, quarterly, and annual forecasts for partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue.
Quota Achievement: Achieve or exceed assigned pipeline, revenue, and partner-development objectives.

sections.title: 3. Partner Enablement and Solution Development — 15%
bullets: Enable Partner Teams: Coordinate with Strategy’s sales, presales, product, enablement, and technical teams to prepare partners to position, demonstrate, sell, and implement Strategy Mosaic and Mosaic AI.

Develop Joint Solutions: Create repeatable public sector solutions and use cases that combine Strategy’s capabilities with partner services, cloud platforms, data technologies, and agency-specific expertise.

Federal Positioning: Help partners communicate Strategy’s value in language that resonates with government stakeholders, including mission outcomes, modernization, cloud adoption, data interoperability, AI governance, security, cost reduction, and operational efficiency.
Sales Support: Assist partners throughout the sales cycle by connecting them with the appropriate Strategy field, presales, product, and leadership resources.
